name: Dune
failureMode: No destruction. Above overwhelmSeverity, absorption is cut to overwhelmedAbsorptionMultiplier for that hazard, but the dune survives to the next one.

name: Sandy Vegetation (Pandanus)
failureMode: No destruction. Weaker physical protection than a Dune, but the cheapest defense on the roster and the best biodiversity return per Coin.
note: absorptionAtMaturity (0.2) is REASONED EXTRAPOLATION, not directly cited (STEP_PROMPT_hazard_science.md Section 1) — Pandanus wasn't in McIvor et al. (2012)'s studied species (that citation is Mangrove's, a different tangled-stilt canopy structure). Kept meaningfully below Mangrove's ceiling (0.55) deliberately; don't raise it toward Mangrove's number without real species-specific wave-attenuation data.

name: Seawall
failureMode: Breaches above failureThreshold: destroyed, redirects unabsorbed surge onward at failureRedirectMultiplier.

name: Mangrove
failureMode: No destruction. Above overwhelmSeverity, absorption is cut to overwhelmedAbsorptionMultiplier for that hazard, but the buffer survives to the next one.
note: PLACEHOLDER money magnitude (STEP_PROMPT_economy_food_yacht.md item 1) — deliberately the smallest of the four money-generating elements (Sand Mining 14 > Beachside Resort 5 > Khazan 2 > Mangrove 1): Mangrove's value proposition is Biodiversity/Food, income is a bonus, not its purpose. Feed into STEP_PROMPT_balance_tuning.md's harness once re-run against this roster.

name: Khazan (Bundh & Sluice)
failureMode: No catastrophic breach. A reservoir, not a wave-attenuator (STEP_PROMPT_hazard_science.md Section 4) — floodBufferCapacityM3 draws down first each Flood event; only once that buffer is exhausted does the old percentage-absorption/graceful-degrade math take over for the overflow. Recovers gradually across subsequent turns, not instantly, so back-to-back floods before it's recovered are meaningfully more dangerous.
note: PLACEHOLDER money magnitude (STEP_PROMPT_economy_food_yacht.md item 1) — nudged 1->2, modest but clearly ahead of Mangrove's 1 without approaching Beachside Resort's 5, reflecting Khazan's already-well-rounded hybrid profile (Biodiversity +2, Food +1). floodBufferCapacityM3 (1500) is a separate PLACEHOLDER (STEP_PROMPT_hazard_science.md Section 4): dimensionally grounded (1 hex = 100m x 100m = 1 hectare; paddy/wetland flood-storage literature — Japan's NARO "paddy-field-dam" studies — puts realistic headroom at ~1,000-2,000 m3/hectare), not a literal measured figure. No longer targets cyclone (Section 2: a reservoir doesn't attenuate wave energy the way vegetation does — Storm Surge Wave defense is Dune/Seawall/Sandy Vegetation/Mangrove only). Feed both numbers into STEP_PROMPT_balance_tuning.md's harness once re-run against this roster.

name: Small Dam
failureMode: STEP_PROMPT_small_dam_reservoir.md: a storage-and-release structure, not a wave-attenuator — floodBufferCapacityM3 draws down first each Flood event, same reservoir mechanic Khazan uses, before absorptionAtMaturity/failureThreshold ever see the input. Breaches above failureThreshold are now tested against the post-buffer overflow severity, not the raw incoming severity: a genuine overtopping destroys the dam and redirects the overflow onward at failureRedirectMultiplier — a dam breach releases what overtopped it, not the raw incoming pulse.
note: PLACEHOLDER money/resilience magnitudes (STEP_PROMPT_visuals_map_river.md item 3 / PROGRESS.md). resilience is POSITIVE as of this pass — earlier revisions had it negative; re-framed as a flood-control structure, not a flood-defense-trading one. floodBufferCapacityM3 (800) is a separate PLACEHOLDER (STEP_PROMPT_small_dam_reservoir.md): deliberately smaller than Khazan's 1500 — a small engineered check-dam on a River tile is a much smaller structure than a hectare-scale wetland/paddy system. absorptionAtMaturity/failureThreshold are unchanged numbers but now exercised against post-buffer overflow rather than raw severity, so failureThreshold's effective trigger rate has shifted — both, plus the new capacity, need a fresh look in STEP_PROMPT_balance_tuning.md's harness once it's re-run against this roster. effects.resilience is forward-compatible data for the not-yet-built zone-based resolution model (GAUNTLET_PROMPT.md v3.0 Section 2/11).

name: Sand Mining
failureMode: No catastrophic breach — it simply offers almost no flood protection (absorptionAtMaturity 0.1, far below Small Dam's 0.75). An untouched river tile is the flood's own source and is skipped entirely (zero damage); building anything on it — Sand Mining included — makes it start taking damage instead, and Sand Mining's near-absent absorption means that damage is close to the full undefended amount.
note: PLACEHOLDER NUMBERS (STEP_PROMPT_visuals_map_river.md item 3): only the direction of each effect is specified (money up, biodiversity down, resilience down). Tuned here — cheaper to build than Small Dam, no maintenance cost, meaningfully higher Money return — so it isn't simply worse than Small Dam in every respect, per that file's explicit balance flag; not a settled/tested number.

name: Yacht
note: PLACEHOLDER buildCost (STEP_PROMPT_economy_food_yacht.md item 4). Purely cosmetic — zero effects, by design (confirm via meterTotal(): every key should read the same with or without a placed Yacht). Should read as a genuine long-run savings target reachable only through several turns of well-managed income, not something a player stumbles into early. Tune alongside the rest of the economy pass in STEP_PROMPT_balance_tuning.md.

name: Breakwater
failureMode: Breaches above failureThreshold: destroyed, redirects unabsorbed surge onward at failureRedirectMultiplier — same engineered-structure failure model as Seawall.
note: STEP_PROMPT_balance_tuning_findings.md Section 3 (decision point, Option B): before this, Coast was permanently undefendable — 18 of 52 Storm-Surge-exposed tiles with zero valid defense, only the purely cosmetic Yacht. A detached/rubble-mound breakwater is a real, established coastal-engineering structure for exactly this exposure (open sea frontage, not a beach/estuary mouth), so this closes a content gap rather than inventing a mechanic. PLACEHOLDER numbers, same convention as every other estimated element on this roster: costed and mainained like Seawall (a comparable engineered marine structure) but with somewhat lower absorptionAtMaturity (0.7 vs 0.9) since a detached breakwater dissipates wave energy rather than fully blocking it, and a proportionally higher failureThreshold (1.25 vs 1.2) reflecting a massive rubble-mound structure's real robustness. Not simulation-tuned — feed into a future balance_sim.ts sweep once Coast coverage is worth testing.
